UltraGreen.ai conducts share buyback of one million shares; CEO ‘remains confident’ on company’s long-term strategy
article:
UltraGreen.ai (SGX:ULG ) announced that it has purchased one million shares from the open market on Aug 24 for a total consideration of US$712,230.39 ($904,861.92).

This translates to an average price of 71.22 US cents. The company conducted the share buyback transaction at a price range of 65.5 US cents and 73 US cents.

Following this latest transaction, UltraGreen owns a total of 2,301,100 treasury shares, which translates to 0.209% of the company’s total issued shares.

On the other hand, UltraGreen’s CEO, Ravinder Sajwan, remains confident in the company’s long-term strategy, competitive position and prospects.

In the announcement dated Aug 24, Sajwan mentioned that UltraGreen has been operating in the fluorescence-guided surgery for more than a decade despite being a relatively young public company.

UltraGreen listed on the Singapore Exchange back on Dec 3, 2025, at an IPO price of US$1.45. With the recent regulatory approval obtained by new entrants, UltraGreen’s share price has witnessed a sharp decline of around 50% from its IPO price.

See also: Geo Energy conducts share buyback with purchase of 637,500 shares from market

“Our commercial response will be calibrated to how new entrants ultimately come to market, including their pricing, distribution approach and customer proposition. Until those commercial plans become clearer, we believe it would be premature to speculate on their potential market impact or the specific actions UltraGreen may take in response,” he states.

Sajwan adds that UltraGreen continues to see significant opportunities for the fluorescence-guided surgery market to expand further.

“I have been purchasing shares in UltraGreen and intend to continue increasing my personal investment in the company. I believe this demonstrates my confidence in the long-term value and prospects of the business and aligns my interests even more closely with those of our shareholders,” Sajwan says.

Shares of UltraGreen closed 8.5 US cents higher, or 13.39% up at 72 US cents on Aug 24.

title: New US$100,000 H-1B fee planned for visa workers already in US
article:
(Aug 24): The Trump administration wants to add an even more expansive US$100,000 fee on the H-1B programme, applying it to individuals hired within the US through regulation after a court blocked a more limited six-figure charge on workers from outside the country.

The new US$103,265 fee would be added to all petitions for H-1B workers subject to an annual statutory cap, including those with master’s degrees. It “would serve as a dedicated revenue mechanism to help recover a portion of the federal government’s costs of administering the lawful immigration system,” according to the proposed rule released Monday.

The Department of Homeland Security’s proposal comes after a court overturned President Donald Trump’s US$100,000 charge for H-1B visa holders hired from outside the country.

That fee, issued through a White House proclamation, disrupted hiring plans for many employers but didn’t apply to students and others approved for H-1B status in the US.

DHS is also reportedly weighing a plan to add a US$100,000 charge for participation in Optional Practical Training, a postgraduate employment programme for foreign students on F-1 visas.

The H-1B programme is limited to 85,000 visa slots each year under a statutory cap, including 20,000 reserved for advanced degree holders. DHS projects fee payments for each cap-subject worker would generate US$8.8 billion annually.

See also: Bessent flags bigger debt buy-back potential, coming US fiscal plan

The new fee would address costs of overseeing the US immigration system at DHS, as well as the departments of Labor, State, and Justice, according to the proposal. It would fund adjudication of benefits, fraud detection and national security vetting, and systems modernisation.

US Citizenship and Immigration Services and the Executive Office of Immigration Review, which houses immigration courts, would be allocated two-thirds of revenue generated by the fee.

DHS said it weighed hiking fees for all immigration applications and petitions but determined that would burden individuals and petitions not connected to employment in the US.

title: Australia to enforce power, water standards for data centres
article:
(Aug 24): Australia will legislate to enforce a national standard on data centres' use of electricity and water as the government aims to harness the technological development to bolster the economy without provoking a backlash.

Australia Prime Minister Anthony Albanese will outline the proposed obligations at a meeting of leaders of all the states and territories on Wednesday. The centre-left government also plans minimum standards for copyright, security and safety for the training of artificial intelligence models.

“Australia can do more to unlock frontier AI development in Australia,” Albanese will say in a speech, according to excerpts released by his office. “And we must shape this change to harness the positive opportunities while minimising the downsides.”

The prime minister’s programme echoes comments from Energy Minister Chris Bowen earlier this month, when he said the government wouldn’t allow “a race to the bottom” in which states and territories are “falling over themselves to attract data centres at the cost of household bills, reliability or emissions.”

On Sunday, Bowen brushed aside the opposition of the state of Queensland, saying “with the right rules in place, you can actually get the investment but actually get to a good outcome where those data centres need to bring their own renewable energy and can back it up with gas peaking.”

Albanese will tell the business community in his speech on Tuesday that “Australia is in a strong position to attract investment in data centres, but maintaining social licence will be essential” to achieve this.

See also: Singapore awards 200MW of data centre capacity across four existing operators

“That means ensuring energy bills do not rise, water security is maintained and locations are appropriate,” he said.

title: Strategy sets up reserve that can be used to buy bitcoin
article:
(Aug 24): Michael Saylor’s Strategy Inc is adding a new pool of cash to its balance-sheet toolkit, part of an effort to preserve flexibility as its once-powerful financing model remains under pressure.

The company said Monday that USD Cash will sit alongside its existing reserve and can be used to buy bitcoin, fund preferred-stock dividends and debt payments, repurchase securities or meet other corporate needs. Strategy said the newly established USD Cash pool currently holds US$1.59 billion.

The original reserve — now US$5.1 billion — may be used only to support the payment of dividends on Strategy’s preferred stock and interest on outstanding indebtedness. Any other use will require board authorisation. The initial reserve was part of a new capital management framework Strategy unveiled in June.

“The new USD Cash pool gives Strategy more time and optionality, but it does not remove those underlying obligations,” said Nicolai Sondergaard, a senior research analyst at Nansen.

Strategy’s shares and debt securities rallied last week as bitcoin ran toward US$80,000, but the financing flywheel remains impaired, with its valuation premium still well below earlier-cycle levels.

The June plan also allowed Strategy to sell bitcoin and repurchase its preferred stocks that have been traded below par. The new framework came as concern over liquidity and shareholder dilution grew amid a prolonged rout in the crypto market.

See also: Bitcoin ETFs see biggest weekly inflow in 10 months during rally

“For MSTR shareholders, the trade-off is dilution in exchange for flexibility,” Sondergaard said. “The latest equity issuance strengthened the balance sheet but did not immediately increase bitcoin-per-share exposure.”

Strategy sold about US$2 billion in common shares over the previous week. The company also repurchased US$136.4 million of its Stretch preferred shares.

Strategy hasn’t bought bitcoin since the seven days ended June 22. It didn’t buy or sell any of the cryptocurrency in the week ended yesterday, according to a filing on Monday. The company holds around US$70 billion in bitcoin.

See also: Bitcoin leaps past US$75,000 as crypto rally continues in Asia

The stock rose as much as 3% to US$122.79 in early trading. It has slumped around 66% in the past year.
